entry.summary: No visa: French law exempts Australians from a short-stay visa for Wallis and Futuna (up to three months in six), except for paid activity that needs French work authorisation.

remote-work.detail: Rechecked 3 November 2026: the Prefecture's entry and stay page covers short-stay visa exemptions and long-stay visas with or without work authorisation (a work contract and the Prefect's approval for salaried work), and Ordinance 2000-371 sets the residence cards; neither names remote work for a foreign employer or a digital nomad visa for a short visit. A long-stay visa without work authorisation needs proof of income to stay without working; it doesn't say whether remote work for a foreign employer counts as working. Easy entry isn't permission to work.
remote-work.next: Ask the Services de l'État in Mata-Utu in writing.

laws.rule: Wallis and Futuna is an overseas collectivity under article 74 of the French Constitution: its own statute sets which French laws apply there, so a French rule may not apply as in mainland France. No visitor-level summary of local laws was found on an official page.
